title: Owner memory is the operating system
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Six staff: owner, four technicians and administrator; plans to hire two more technicians.
owner_narrative: I coordinate everything through messages and memory. When I took three days away, someone revisited a customer before the part arrived, and invoices stopped because nobody knew what I promised. We have spreadsheets and calendars, but I connect them in my head.
current_workflow: Owner tells office what to bill

diagnostic_interview.question: Which commitments exist only in your head?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Call-before-visit rules, parts approvals and invoice holds.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Some decisions legitimately require the owner’s commercial judgement; do not automate every escalation or assume full delegation is desired.

diagnostic_interview.question: Which decisions can staff safely make?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Routine scheduling and approved parts use, but spending limits are unwritten.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Why did the premature visit happen?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Nobody could see the pending part dependency.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Missing next-action visibility, not technician competence.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: How much implementation time is realistic?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Short daily reviews; no lengthy parallel data entry.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: A simulated message contains a parts promise absent from the calendar.
A simulated invoice has an owner-only hold condition.
A simulated absence review identifies repeated routine questions.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Commitments, dependencies and delegated authority are person-bound rather than recorded in a shared workflow.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: Some decisions legitimately require the owner’s commercial judgement; do not automate every escalation or assume full delegation is desired.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Create one lightweight commitment board with owner, next action and blocker; publish agreed routine decision boundaries.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Capture message-derived task drafts for confirmation; remind responsible staff about dependencies; escalate exceptions beyond agreed authority.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Extracted promises remain drafts until confirmed.
requirements.rationale: Commitments, dependencies and delegated authority are person-bound rather than recorded in a shared workflow.

requirements.statement: Invoice holds require an explicit release decision.
requirements.rationale: Commitments, dependencies and delegated authority are person-bound rather than recorded in a shared workflow.

requirements.statement: A missing part blocks a visit that requires it.
requirements.rationale: Commitments, dependencies and delegated authority are person-bound rather than recorded in a shared workflow.

requirements.statement: Decisions beyond authority escalate instead of guessing.
requirements.rationale: Commitments, dependencies and delegated authority are person-bound rather than recorded in a shared workflow.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: Pending part prevents a misleading ready-to-visit state.
Staff can handle an approved routine decision during owner absence.
A complaint hold survives unrelated job completion.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Commitment extraction and a formal delegation matrix require new rules and review.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Owner interruptions for routine decisions per staffed day; track overdue commitments and incorrect delegated decisions.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Create one lightweight commitment board with owner, next action and blocker; publish agreed routine decision boundaries. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: Some decisions legitimately require the owner’s commercial judgement; do not automate every escalation or assume full delegation is desired.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Actual delegation limits and which promises are binding require the owner’s review.
